It is not a dead end: the GitHub MCP tool GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES (owner kavopdf, repo app, branch main, upserts=[{path,content,encoding:utf-8}]) commits several files atomically and worked for all four commits of this run. context: The folio fix is IN the engine and it works: a page's own page number is no longer table content. PdfToWord.markFolios marks the glyphs of a folio drawn in the bottom band (same shapes as DocxWriter.isFolio), and buildTables, tableFromCells and the 'is this line inside a table' flow test all refuse them; DocxWriter.anchorBox no longer lets the horizontal clamp slide a folio off its own x. 041122 page 7 went from 11 sheets to 10 (source 9), the folio lands at x=584.2 against the source's 584.1, and no word is lost on any page. Blast radius measured corpus-wide by converting all 213 documents with and without the change and diffing document.xml: exactly 3 documents differ (041122, Account_Opening_Form_Fillable_filled, itr-computation-with-slab-table) - the other 210 are byte-identical. The attempt is recorded as reverted because the class number did not move: share5 86.38 -> 86.18 on the two forms. THE REASON IS NOT THIS CHANGE - read the next field. Also: the committed RANKING.csv is STALE. It says 041122 is 97.62 and 392_statistical_console_output is 1.61; the PRISTINE engine from main (git clone, no change of mine) measures 86.38 and 28.39 on the same corpus, doc for doc. So gate.py's 'REGRESSION: 54 documents worse than baseline' is not about this run's change - it is 54 documents of drift between the committed file and the corpus the file is compared against. A fresh RANKING.csv measured on this corpus is committed with this round; the next run compares against that.
